metadata.title: When Claude Audits a Spreadsheet, Does It Fix Anything?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude finds AND fixes spreadsheet errors when it audits one -- or is doing something narrower. Lands the carry-out that audit-xls checks balance first, flags suspect formulas by cell, and never rewrites one -- fixing stays with the human.
metadata.source_note: Source sheet's narration carries real skill-specific facts (not unfilled template placeholders) -- see QUESTION.md. Facts preserved: the audit-xls skill audits a spreadsheet for formula accuracy, errors, and common mistakes; scopes to a selected range, a single sheet, or the entire model; checks BS balance first because everything downstream is suspect if it's off; triggers on phrases like 'audit this sheet' / 'check my formulas' / 'model won't balance'. beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that asking Claude to audit a spreadsheet means it finds the errors and fixes them while it's in there. But the skill doesn't work that way. It audits a spreadsheet for formula accuracy, errors, and common mistakes, and reports what it finds — cited by cell. Give it a sheet with a formula you already know is broken, and check the sheet again after: the formula is untouched. What changed is the report, not the spreadsheet.

shot.new_visual_element: A 'fix it' hand reaching for a broken cell, struck through; a report card citing the same cell, lit

production_viz.label: Fix, struck -- report, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a hand icon labelled 'FIX IT' reaching toward a cell marked with an error glyph. Right: a numbered card labelled 'AUDIT REPORT' listing 'cell: formula error, cited'. The fix-it side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the report side stays lit. A final line reads 'checked again -- cell unchanged' beside the same cell, still showing the original broken formula.

beats.narration_text: What it actually checks, and in what order: BS balance first — if the balance sheet doesn't balance, everything downstream is suspect. Watch the anchor: a balance sheet off by a fixed amount. It's checked first, the mismatch is found, the affected cells are cited, and a finding is reported. Then it stops — nothing is rewritten.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- a balance sheet mismatch traveling checked-first -> found -> cited -> reported, then stopping

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one mismatch, four stops
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labelled 'SCOPE SET', 'BS CHECKED FIRST', 'MISMATCH FOUND', 'CITED, REPORTED'. A single highlighted token 'BS OFF BY $1,200' travels down through all four cards in turn, each lighting as it arrives. At the bottom, the token halts beside a label 'nothing rewritten' -- it does not continue past the reported card. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS, PAID OFF, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: So back to that balance sheet: reported, cited, waiting for you to look. But a clean BS-balance pass doesn't mean the whole model in scope is error-free — it only clears that one check; formula errors elsewhere are checked separately. And a BS-imbalance flag doesn't mean every downstream number is individually wrong — it means they're unverified until the imbalance is resolved, not confirmed incorrect. Either way, nothing in the sheet has been changed.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, cited and reported; splits into 'balanced is not error-free' and 'suspect is not wrong'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- reported, then split
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 FOUR-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical placement, the token resting at the 'CITED, REPORTED' card beside 'nothing rewritten'. It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left reads 'BS: OK' with a checkmark, then a struck-through 'ERROR-FREE?' beneath it, labelled 'balanced is not error-free'; right reads 'BS: OFF' beside a faint 'unverified, not confirmed' note, labelled 'suspect is not wrong'.

beats.narration_text: audit-xls checks the balance sheet first, then flags every suspect formula by cell — but it never rewrites one. Finding the problem is Claude's job here; fixing it stays yours.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Give Claude a spreadsheet with one formula you already know is wrong, and ask it to run the audit-xls skill: check balance first, then scan for formula errors, and report what it finds by cell. Then open the sheet afterward and check whether the formula itself changed. Liam, in for Bear.
